strengths: Significance: PMVB offers a simple way to integrate predictions into existing MIP solvers through cardinality constraints. Exploring all four complementary regions preserves exactness, while solving the preferred region alone provides a useful primal heuristic.

Originality: The risk-pooling interpretation and separate budgets for errors among predicted zeros and ones offer an interesting perspective on prediction-guided local branching. The LP-based variant also addresses settings without historical training data.

Evaluation: The experiments cover logistic regression, GNNs, two commercial solvers, several combinatorial problem families, and simulated unit commitment. Table 2 reports 1.11–1.31× speedups for exact solving, suggesting practical potential.

Presentation, reproducibility, and limitations: The overall workflow and pseudocode are accessible, and the manuscript supplies dataset descriptions, hardware information, and a code link. It appropriately acknowledges the strong independence assumption and possible infeasibility of restricted neighborhoods. No material research-ethics concern is evident.
weaknesses: Soundness—Theorem 2.1: Equation (4) incorrectly transfers the marginal prediction-accuracy guarantee of Lemma 2.1 to variables selected by the instance-dependent predictions. High overall accuracy does not imply high accuracy conditional on predicting one or zero; a classifier can make exclusively incorrect positive predictions while remaining highly accurate overall. The random sets U and L therefore cannot be treated as fixed collections with the asserted expectation bounds. Assumption A4 does not supply the missing conditional guarantees, so the central Hoeffding argument is unsupported.

Soundness—practical probability guarantees: Theorem 3.1 is a valid Chebyshev argument when the population conditions in (9) and (10) hold, but the manuscript does not establish these conditions from finite validation data or specify the experimental variance bounds. This is especially unclear for the data-free setting. The stronger constraints in Remark 3.1 also do not inherit the guarantee without additional calibration assumptions. No empirical coverage assessment is reported, and some training labels allow 10% optimality gaps despite the theory targeting optimal solutions.

Soundness—Theorem 4.1: The proof bounds the number of LP-selected items omitted by the integer optimum, then asserts that the opposite inequality follows by taking complements. Knapsack solutions need not have equal cardinality, so a bound on |U\U*| does not imply the same bound on |U*\U|. The proof also uses separate high-probability events for weights and ratios without accounting for their joint failure probability. The stated result needs a corrected proof.

Evaluation: Section 5.4 retains only 57 of the initial 132 MIPLIB instances after excluding infeasible restricted problems and joint timeouts. Consequently, the reported 16% improvement describes a selected subset rather than overall performance. Section 5.2 measures time to PMVB's own achieved target without complementary fixed-budget solution-quality results or clear failure handling. These choices limit interpretation of the large heuristic speedups; uncertainty estimates are also absent, with only five SCUC test instances per setting.

Originality and attribution: The manuscript acknowledges existing local/cardinality branching and prediction-based distance constraints, but compares principally against unmodified solvers. Comparisons with prediction-guided local branching using the same predictor, and ablations of probabilistic versus fixed neighborhood budgets, are needed to establish what the proposed construction adds. With the probability guarantees unresolved, its distinct contribution remains insufficiently supported.

Reproducibility and presentation: The MKP generator in Section 5.1 specifies capacities proportional to (1/(4n)) times each row sum. Under the stated coefficient distribution and dimensions, this would usually yield trivial all-zero optima, which is difficult to reconcile with the reported hard MKP instances and requires clarification. Solver versions, random seeds, and whether timings include prediction and LP-processing overhead are also unspecified.
